brief: A hotter-than-expected US core CPI print pushed Treasury yields higher and kept European sovereign spreads wide on French and Italian fiscal concerns, but GS still sees a directional bias toward lower G4 yields. Yields staying near current levels would cut US growth by about 0.5pp and DM growth by 0.4-0.6pp next year (GS's 2027 baseline shows a 0.2pp drag, more than double if rates persist); a further sharp yield rise would pressure equities and credit, especially with higher rate volatility. GS shifted overweight bonds in its 12m allocation and overweight equities in its 3m allocation on earnings growth and lower valuations, and still favors equities over bonds near and medium term. Separately, EM equity concentration from the AI investment boom reflects profit growth, not speculation, so GS recommends a differentiated regional approach (North Asia, India, LatAm, CEE) with derivative hedges. On elections, US prediction markets favor a Democratic midterm sweep on gas prices; GS cut its USD/BRL forecast ahead of Brazil's October 25 runoff; Le Pen leads French 2027 polling but her fiscal plan faces implementation hurdles; UK growth slows this winter but improves in 2027 as gas falls and the BoE eases less than priced.
